title: Google tests a Flipkart 'Buy' button inside Gemini and AI Mode in India
subtitle: A small pilot in three product categories lets Indian shoppers complete a Flipkart checkout without leaving Google's AI interface, ahead of the country's festive shopping season.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google confirmed this week that it is piloting a Flipkart-branded 'Buy' button inside Gemini and AI Mode for a subset of users in India. The test covers three product categories — smartphones, other consumer electronics, and mobile accessories — and lets a shopper who lands on a Flipkart product listing inside an AI answer tap through to a Flipkart-branded checkout flow that runs inside Google's AI interface. A wider rollout is planned for October, before India's Diwali-season shopping peak.

The pilot runs on Google's Universal Commerce Protocol, an open specification the company introduced earlier this year so AI agents can transact with retailers over a standard interface rather than screen-scraping. That matters because it is the mechanism, not the announcement, that would let Google generalize this beyond Flipkart. India is a useful launch site: Google already owns a minority stake in Flipkart from a 2024 investment round led by Walmart, festive-quarter e-commerce volumes are large and concentrated, and the country is one of Gemini's fastest-growing markets.

The move fits a pattern from the last three weeks of agentic-commerce launches — OpenAI's international ChatGPT ads with Shopify sponsored agents earlier this week, Anthropic's Claude commerce agents with Shopify, Visa and Mastercard in early September, and Ant Group's cross-border KYA agent identity work with Visa and Mastercard on September 13. What is new here is that the transaction completes inside the AI chat, not in a handoff back to the retailer's app. That is closer to the version of agentic commerce that platform incumbents are trying to own and that regulators are starting to notice.

For learners: this is a good moment to look up the phrase 'agentic commerce protocol' and read one primary spec — Google's UCP, Anthropic's commerce agents description, or Visa's Trusted Agent framework. The interesting design questions are unglamorous: how does an AI agent authenticate a purchase, how are refunds and disputes handled when the buyer never touched the retailer's site, and who is responsible if the agent misreads a product page? Those answers, more than any single Gemini feature, will decide how much of your future online shopping runs through a chat window.
